content:
Garment Stand collar quilted jacket, fully lined

Level Intermediate

Sizes XXS – 4XL

Fabric Quilted cotton, wool, tweed, twill

Pieces 15

This free quilted jacket sewing pattern makes a fitted, fully lined jacket with a soft stand collar, a row of buttons down the front and two rounded patch pockets. Princess seams shape it front and back, and it finishes just below the hip, so it works as a light autumn layer or a cosy winter jacket in wool.

→ Jump to the free download

1 cm (3/8″) seam allowance · 4 cm (1 5/8″) hem included

Get the pattern

Free PDF pattern, with one file per size, XXS to 4XL (US 00–22). Share your make with #sewcraftly!

Download A4
Download US Letter

Print page 1 at 100% and check that the test square measures 10 cm (4 in). New to PDF patterns? Read how to print and assemble a PDF pattern.

Sizing guide

Choose your size by your bust, waist and hip measurements, then check the finished measurements for the ease you like. The jacket has about 9 cm (3 1/2″) of ease at the bust in size 8. If your quilted fabric is thicker than 5 mm (3/16″), or you want to wear the jacket over a warm sweater, go one size up. Not sure? Read how to choose your size.

Letter sizes: 00 = XXS · 0/2 = XS · 4/6 = S · 8/10 = M · 12/14 = L · 16 = XL · 18 = 2XL · 20 = 3XL · 22 = 4XL

Body measurements

Finished garment measurements

Chest, waist, low hip, hem and upper arm are full circumferences of the closed jacket, measured on the pattern without seam allowances. Back length is measured at centre back; sleeve length along the upper sleeve, from the top of the cap to the hem. Drafted for a height of 168 cm (5′6″).

Fabric and notions

Fabric amounts were calculated by laying out every piece of each size single layer, plus about 8 %. Add about 10 % for a one-way print. If you quilt your own fabric, quilt about 10 % more than the main fabric amount, then cut the pieces from the quilted panels.

Common fit adjustments

Length. The jacket is drafted for a height of 168 cm (5′6″), with a back length of about 73 cm (28 3/4″). Cut and spread, or overlap, every body piece and lining piece by the same amount between the waist and the hem, below the pocket position. Change the sleeve length above the vent on all four sleeve pieces.

Thick quilting. Size up if your quilted fabric is more than 5 mm thick, trim the batting out of every seam allowance and use a walking foot.

Materials

  • Main fabric: 2.0 to 2.5 m (2 1/4 to 2 3/4 yd) of 150 cm wide fabric: pre-quilted cotton or a patchwork quilt you make yourself, medium-weight wool, boiled wool or tweed, or cotton twill, canvas or corduroy for spring
  • Lining: 1.4 to 1.5 m (1 5/8 to 1 3/4 yd) of viscose (rayon) twill, cupro or acetate lining; cotton lawn also works with quilted cotton
  • Fusible interfacing: 0.9 to 1.1 m for quilted fabric (facings and stand only), 2.5 to 3.0 m for wool
  • Buttons: 6 front buttons of 1.5 cm (5/8″), plus 1 more for the stand (as in our photo), and 6 small buttons of 1 cm (3/8″) for the sleeve vents
  • Shoulder pads (optional): 1 pair, 1 cm (3/8″) thick
  • All-purpose thread, a walking foot for quilted fabric, a hand-sewing needle, clips and a tailor’s ham

Pattern pieces

  • 1 Front lining, lining: cut 2
  • 2 Center front and 3 Side front, main + interfacing: cut 2 + 2 each
  • 4 Center back, main + interfacing: cut 2 + 2
  • 5 Center back lining, lining: cut 1
  • 6 Side back, main + interfacing: cut 2 + 2
  • 7 Side back lining, lining: cut 2
  • 8 Front neck facing and 9 Back neck facing, main + interfacing: cut 2 + 2 and 1 + 1
  • 10 Collar stand, main + interfacing: cut 2 + 2
  • 11 Patch pocket, main: cut 2
  • 12 Upper sleeve and 13 Lower sleeve, main: cut 2 each
  • 14 Upper sleeve lining and 15 Lower sleeve lining: cut 2 each

The center back lining and the collar stand are drawn whole: cut them single layer, not on a fold. Transfer the buttons and buttonholes, the pocket box, the lining pleat lines and the FOLD mark on the front lining.

New to PDF patterns? Start here

Our free step-by-step guides take you from your measurements to a printed pattern:

  1. How to take your body measurements: what to measure and how, in 10 minutes.
  2. How to choose your size: which measurement to follow, and what to do between sizes.
  3. How to print and assemble your pattern: A4 or US Letter, the test box, and taping the pages.

Design details and fit of the quilted jacket

The Stand Collar Quilted Jacket is a neat, collarless-looking jacket with a soft stand that frames the neck. It is fully lined, and the lining is bagged by machine, so there is no hand hemming. In our photo it is made in a burgundy quilted cotton with mixed quilting patterns and wooden buttons.

  • Soft stand collar, with an optional 7th button on the stand
  • Front button closure with 6 buttons
  • Princess seams front and back, plus a center back seam
  • Two rounded patch pockets on the side fronts
  • Two-piece sleeves with a 3-button vent
  • Full lining with front facings, back neck facing and a back ease pleat
  • Length just below the hip, with a gently flared hem

The fit is close through the waist and eases out over the hips, so the jacket looks tailored but still layers over a fine knit or a shirt.

Sewing notes

Fit & style

Fitted at the waist, just below the hip. Size up for thick quilting.

Fabrics

Quilted cotton, patchwork quilts, medium wool, tweed, twill or corduroy, with a smooth lining.

Cutting & sewing

Walking foot, 3–3.5 mm stitch, clips instead of pins, and trim the batting from every seam.

Choosing fabric for a quilted jacket

For the look of our photo, use a pre-quilted cotton, or make your own quilted panels from a cotton top, a thin batting and a cotton backing. Thin batting matters: a quilt thicker than about 5 mm makes the princess seams and the stand bulky. A quilt coat made from an old patchwork quilt also works well, as long as the fabric is still strong.

For a classic winter jacket, choose a medium-weight wool, boiled wool or tweed and interface all the shell pieces. Cotton twill, canvas or corduroy give a lighter spring version. For the lining, viscose twill, cupro or acetate slide over your clothes; cotton lawn is a soft choice inside a quilted cotton jacket.

Printable sewing tutorial

Need help completing the project?

Get the full printable tutorial for the Stand Collar Quilted Jacket: detailed step-by-step sewing instructions with clear illustrations, line sketches, a sizing guide and the list of materials you need.

  • Illustrated diagrams for every step, from the patch pockets to the bagged lining
  • Size charts, finished measurements and fabric amounts per size
  • Video guides for the key techniques, with links and QR codes

Sewing steps

Seam allowance 1 cm (3/8″) unless stated otherwise, 1.5 cm (5/8″) on the patch pockets. Sew right sides together and press every seam before crossing it with another one. With quilted fabric, trim the batting out of each seam allowance after stitching.

  1. Prepare and interface. Fuse interfacing to the shell pieces, facings and stands (for quilted fabric, only pieces 8, 9 and 10), overlock the quilted edges and staystitch the necklines.
  2. Prepare the patch pockets. Fold and stitch the top edge, gather the rounded corners with long stitches and press the sides and bottom under.
  3. Sew the pockets on. Place each pocket in its box on the side front, edgestitch it and reinforce the top corners.
  4. Front princess seams. Join each side front to its center front, clip the curve and press open over a ham.
  5. Back seams. Sew the center back seam, then the side backs, and press open.
  6. Shoulders and sides. Sew the shoulder and side seams and press them open.
  7. Sleeves and vent. Sew the back sleeve seam down to the vent, pivot across the extension, then sew the front sleeve seam.
  8. Set in the sleeves. Ease the caps into the armholes and stitch with the sleeve on top.
  9. Outer collar stand. Sew the outer stand to the jacket neckline, ends on the front edges.
  10. Lining pleat and fold. Baste the back ease pleat and the small fold on each front lining, then join the lining backs.
  11. Facings and lining body. Sew the facings to the lining and join the lining at the shoulders and sides.
  12. Lining sleeves. Sew the lining sleeves, leaving a 20 cm opening in one, and set them into the lining.
  13. Inner collar stand. Sew the second stand to the neck edge of the facings.
  14. Join jacket and lining. Stitch the lining unit to the jacket in one seam along the fronts and around the stand, then trim, grade, understitch and turn.
  15. Body hem. Sew the lining to the jacket hem and fold the 4 cm hem up, leaving a small ease fold in the lining.
  16. Sleeve hems. Join each sleeve and its lining at the hem, fold up the 4 cm hem and finish the vent by hand.
  17. Turn and close. Turn the jacket through the sleeve lining opening, close it and press all the edges through a cloth.
  18. Buttonholes and buttons. Make 6 buttonholes on the right front (plus one on the stand if you like) and sew on the front and sleeve buttons.

Tips and common mistakes

Bulky seams. With quilted fabric, trim the batting out of every seam allowance close to the stitching, so the princess seams and the stand lie flat.

Shifting layers. Use a walking foot, a 3–3.5 mm stitch and clips rather than pins, which leave holes and slip out of thick layers.

Lumpy pocket curves. Pull the gathering threads before pressing the rounded corners, and trim the batting out of the folded allowance first.

Flattened quilting. Press through a cloth with steam and pat with your hand: never press hard on the quilted surface.

Test buttonholes. Make a test buttonhole on a scrap with all the layers, including batting and interfacing, before you sew the real ones.

How to style the quilted jacket

Everyday: with cream wide-leg trousers and loafers, like in our photo, or with straight jeans and a white tee for the weekend.

Smarter: in plain wool with a contrast lining over a fine knit and a midi skirt for the office.

More to sew: for a hooded version, try our quilted hooded jacket sewing pattern, or for a wool jacket with the same princess lines, our princess seam jacket sewing pattern.

Care

Follow the care of your main fabric and lining. Wash quilted cotton cool on a gentle cycle and dry it flat; dry clean wool or hand wash it cold. Press through a cloth, on the lining side.

Questions

Is seam allowance included?

Yes: 1 cm (3/8″) everywhere except the patch pockets (1.5 cm / 5/8″), plus a 4 cm (1 5/8″) hem on the body and sleeves.

Which paper sizes are included?

The free download comes in A4 and US Letter, as a printable PDF with one file per size, XXS to 4XL (US 00–22).

Which size should I choose?

Choose by your bust, waist and hip measurements and check the finished measurements. Take one size up for thick quilting or to wear the jacket over a warm sweater.

Can I make it from an old quilt?

Yes, as long as the quilt is thin (about 5 mm or less) and the fabric is still strong. Lay out all the pieces first: you need about the same amount as the main fabric, plus 10 %.

Is the jacket lined?

Yes, it is fully lined. The lining is bagged by machine, with a back ease pleat, so there is no hand hemming.

How many buttons do I need?

6 front buttons of 1.5 cm (5/8″), 1 more if you want a button on the stand, and 6 small buttons of 1 cm (3/8″) for the sleeve vents.

Is this jacket good for beginners?

It is an intermediate project. The trickiest part is joining the jacket and the lining along the front edges and the stand, then the hems: go slowly and pin well.
